newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA'S BULBANK RAISES CAPITAL BY $100 MLN.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA'S BULBANK RAISES CAPITAL BY $100 MLN.

text.p: Bulgaria's Bulbank will raise its capital by $100 million to 277.3 billion levs from 15.1 billion levs in a bid to offset erosion of its shares' value by the weakening lev, its chairman said on Thursday.
"Bulbank's shareholders decided today to raise the bank's capital to 277.3 billion levs from 15.1 billion levs through transforming liabilities into capital," Chavdar Kanchev told reporters.
The capital raise will be covered by dollar-denominated bad debt bonds, known as Zunks with $158 million par value.
The Zunks, issued by the state three years ago to cover bad loans of state firms, were given to Bulbank in 1994 to fill a gap caused by transformation of debts owed to the bank by state firms.
The capital raise could be estimated at $100 million if the central bank accepted denomination of bank capital in foreign currency, Kanchev said.

Under an agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), sealed last week, Bulgaria pledges to accept bank capital denominated in foreign currency. So far the central bank accepted registrations of bank capital in the national currency, the lev.
"The capital raise aims to compensate the bank's shareholders, against any devaluation of their stake," Kanchev said.
The lev nosedived against the dollar from 70.7 at the end of 1995 to 3,000 per dollar in February. It recovered to around 1,500 now.
Bulgaria's Bank Cosolidation Company (BCC) which manages state equity in local commercial banks holds 98.03 percent in Bulbank.
Under the capital raise due to be registered by the end of 1997, current shareholders would receive 52 new shares against each old share.
Bulbank's registered and paid-in capital stood at 5.042 billion levs at the end of 1996, showed its balance sheet.
Bulbank has transformed 10.1 billion levs from its 1996 net-profit to raise the capital from five billion levs to 15.1 billion levs, said Kanchev.
Bulbank's posted 12.4 billion levs net-profit in 1996 after setting aside provisions against risk assets of 163.9 billion levs and paying 9.6 billion levs in taxes on 185.7 billion levs gross profit.
Under the first capital raise to 15.1 billion levs, each shareholder will receive two new shares against an old one.
The shareholders also decided to distribute a ten percent dividend on 504 million levs from the 1996 net-profit, said Kanchev.

Bulbank's assets totaled 1.349 trillion levs ($2.77 billion) at the end of 1996, which compares to 1.255 trillion levs ($2.57 billion) assets of the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB), BNB and Bulbank balance figures showed.

A stake in Bulbank will be offered for sale in line with Bulgaria's pledges privatise its six state-owned banks mid- 1998. Bulbank also renamed itself to Bulbank LTD, abandoning its previous name Bulgarian Foreign Trade Bank (BFTB). -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
